trust_decision.summary: Whether a media file may be written under an executable extension is decided in FileHandler::getFilePath(): it matches the blacklist against the raw original filename case-sensitively and only afterwards lowercases the extension it stores, so 'webshell.pHp' passes the check and lands on disk as 'webshell.php'.

landing_point.why: The report says 'extension blacklist bypass on upload', and this private getFilePath() is the only place in the tree where the blacklisted_extensions option is consulted before the stored name is built.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST admin media create (/create/{folderId}/{type}), modal create (/create/modal/{folderId}/{type}), media edit (/media/{mediaId}), drop upload (/media/drop/{folderId}); public service kunstmaan_media.media_handlers.file / MediaCreatorService::createFile()

fix_sites.entry_point: kernel config tree: kunstmaan_media.blacklisted_extensions defaults + new kunstmaan_media.allowed_extensions (config load, no HTTP route)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: RenameSoftDeletedCommand is an operator-run console maintenance command for already soft-deleted media, not an upload route, so the upload blacklist can be argued not to apply to it; the default extension list is deployment configuration, so the check itself 'looks fixed'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate media names must keep working: a double extension such as 'evil.php.jpg' must still be stored as 'evil-php.jpg' (the slugifier rewrites the inner dot of the filename part, the final .jpg is kept), an allow-listed mixed-case extension such as 'holiday.JPG' must still become 'holiday.jpg', and a file with no extension ('README') must be stored as 'readme' with no trailing dot. An over-broad fix that rewrites any name containing an executable token, or that appends '.txt'/a dot when there is no extension, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: other server-executable extensions: phtml, php5, phar, phps, pht, shtml, cgi, asp, jsp
filename with no extension: README -> readme
optional allow-list configured (allowed_extensions) on top of the blacklist, and its empty default

O8_uncovered_routes.route: kuma:media:rename-soft-deleted --original renames a soft-deleted media file back to $media->getOriginalFilename() verbatim, so an upload that the blacklist stored as '<uuid>/webshell.txt' is renamed to '<uuid>/webshell.php' inside public/uploads/media; no blacklist/allow-list/slugify is applied on this path
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a CLI maintenance command for soft-deleted media that an operator runs by hand, not an upload route, so it can be read as outside the advisory's upload protection.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another file and namespace (Command/) in the same bundle, reached only from the console application; no shared call with the fixed getFilePath()

O8b_injection_room.sibling: per-handler cleanup/sanitise step on the same rename/remove family of commands
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already sits next to RenameSoftDeletedCommand and iterates the same media set through MediaManager::removeMedia, so a maintainer adding a name-sanitising helper would plausibly add a third command or extend this one.
PdfHandler and ImageHandler already override saveMedia()/prepareMedia() on top of FileHandler, so a maintainer fixing 'the file handler' can reasonably extend this subclass instead of the base class.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: URL/name composition from the uploaded file's own extension (mediaPath . uuid . '.' . getExtension())
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the second place in the same directory that turns an upload into a served name, so a fix written by someone reading FileHelper first would be planted there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: compiler pass injecting blacklist/allow-list defaults into every tagged media handler instead of per-service YAML calls
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every handler is registered by tag here, so centralising the option injection in this pass is a natural refactor a maintainer could have made.

O9_family: unrestricted file upload of executable content into the web root (CWE-434), stored-file RCE
